topic: How does the 14.6% bandwidth affect frequency planning for multi-satellite networks with adjacent channel interference risks?
consensus_response: The 14.6% bandwidth affects frequency planning by limiting available spectrum, increasing interference risks in multi-satellite networks. In Ku-band (14.0-14.5 GHz), adaptive filtering can dynamically adjust frequencies to minimize adjacent channel interference, but this requires significant computational resources. Machine learning-based interference mitigation can further optimize channel usage by predicting and adapting to changing conditions. However, it demands substantial data processing power. Cognitive radio enables adaptive frequency allocation based on real-time network conditions, optimizing spectral efficiency while minimizing interference risks.
